## Locality Guide: Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota (1890–1920)

### Jurisdictional Context
Benson County organized 9 March 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties (Dakota Territory). North Dakota statehood: 2 November 1889. County seat: Minnewaukan. No courthouse disasters recorded.

Neighboring counties: Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, Wells.

### Vital Records
- **Birth (statewide):** 1907 (compliance 1924). County: 'late 1890s' (physical only, courthouse). FamilySearch has not acquired ND birth records. An 1898 birth certificate may exist at the courthouse but is not online.
- **Death (statewide):** 1907 (compliance 1924). County: 1895 (physical, courthouse).
- **Marriage (statewide):** 1925. County: late 1800s. FS coll. 2550852 (1872–2000), indexed + images.

### Census Records
- 1890 federal: destroyed — no records survive for ND.
- **1900 federal: 92% name-indexed on FamilySearch** (vol. 004120517_002_M9LK-PZ1) — primary access point for parentage research.
- 1910 federal: available via standard FS record search.
- **1915 ND state census: FS coll. 2346284** (51–55% indexed); also vols. 007637091, 007637092.
- 1925 ND state census: FS coll. 2351024.

### Church Records
Lutheran churches dominant (Norwegian settlement). Flora Lutheran Church (vol. 100881427, 34% indexed, English/Norwegian) and Esmond Lutheran Church (vol. 100881428, 36% indexed) are on FamilySearch. Also: US ELCA Church Records 1875–1940 on Ancestry (coll. 60722).

### Naturalization Records
Benson County volumes 007785641–007785645 on FamilySearch: 0% name-indexed, full-text searchable. Span 1884–1955. Also FS coll. 3241359 (1868–1924), indexed + images.

### Land and Homestead
BLM GLO Records (glorecords.blm.gov) for patents/homesteads. Ancestry: U.S. Homestead Records 1863–1908. USGenWeb Benson County BLM Land Records Index.

### Probate
Benson County probate from 1883 (courthouse). Ancestry: ND & SD Wills and Probate 1800–1985.

### Obituaries and Newspapers
NDSU Obituary Index; Genealogy Trails Benson County obituaries; Chronicling America; GenealogyBank.

### External Repositories
- Benson County Courthouse, 311 B Ave Street, Minnewaukan ND 58351 (701.473.5345)
- North Dakota State Archives (pre-1925 marriage index; microfilm)
- North Dakota State University Archives (biography index, obituary index, naturalization index)
- State Historical Society of North Dakota (marriage records online index)

entry.rationale: The 1900 federal census is the single highest-value source for this question. Reuben Spencer Spriggs was born 6 November 1898; in June 1900 he would appear as an infant (age 1) in his parents' household, with the head of household relationship naming both parents directly. FamilySearch volume 004120517_002_M9LK-PZ1 covers Benson County at 92% name-indexed — the best digitization level available for this county and period. The 1890 census was destroyed and does not exist for North Dakota (per loc_001). Search under surname variants Spriggs and Sprigs. This is free, indexed, and has the highest probability of immediately naming both parents.

The 1910 federal census will show Reuben at age 11, almost certainly still in his parents' household. This corroborates any parents identified in 1900, adds each parent's age, birthplace, and parents' birthplaces (columns added in 1900 and retained in 1910), and may reveal siblings. If the family relocated or Reuben's surname differs from a parent's (stepparent scenario), the 1910 census will flag it. Search Benson County; also check neighboring Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, Eddy, and Wells counties if not found in Benson.

North Dakota conducted a state census in 1915 (FamilySearch collection 2346284, 51–55% indexed; also vols. 007637091 and 007637092). Reuben would be ~16 and likely still in the household. The state census lists relationship to head of household and can confirm the parental household established by 1900 and 1910. If Reuben has left home by 1915, the parents' household will still be searchable and can corroborate their names and ages.

Dedicated parentage-question item for the candidate parents' marriage to each other. FamilySearch collection 2550852 (North Dakota, County Marriages, 1872–2000) covers Benson County with index and images. The parents' marriage record will supply the mother's maiden name (if this was her first marriage), confirm the father's given name, and establish that they were a couple before Reuben's November 1898 birth. Date range 1880–1910 spans the plausible pre-birth window (parents could have married as early as the 1880s if older) plus a small buffer. If the parents are identified in the 1900 census, use those names to search this collection. Statewide marriage registration did not begin until 1925; county records from 'late 1800s' are captured in this collection (per loc_001).

The dominant religious group in Benson County was Norwegian/Scandinavian Lutheran (per loc_001). Two digitized Lutheran church volumes cover the county on FamilySearch: Flora Lutheran Church (vol. 100881427, 34% indexed, English/Norwegian, 1820–1997) and Esmond Lutheran Church (vol. 100881428, 36% indexed, English/Norwegian, 1830–1958). A baptism entry for Reuben Spencer Spriggs (Nov 1898) would name both parents and is direct parentage evidence. The parents' church marriage record (if different from the civil record in pli_004) may also name the mother's father. Browse both volumes; also search the ELCA Records collection on Ancestry (coll. 60722, 1875–1940) which includes Flora Lutheran Church. Note: records are partially in Norwegian — read for patronymic naming conventions if found.

Statewide birth registration began in 1907; county-level records begin 'late 1890s' and are held physically at the Benson County Clerk District Court, 311 B Ave Street, Minnewaukan, ND 58351, phone 701.473.5345 (per loc_001). A birth record for Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, may exist there — compliance was low in the late 1890s but not zero. FamilySearch Library has not acquired ND birth records. This requires a direct courthouse inquiry or mail request. Lower probability than census, but if it exists it is direct, original, and names both parents.

FAN item to identify and locate the father. When North Dakota opened for settlement, most land in Benson County was acquired through federal homestead or land patent. The BLM General Land Office Records (glorecords.blm.gov) and USGenWeb Benson County BLM Land Records Index list federal patents by patentee name; a search for Spriggs (and variants) in Benson County will locate any land entry the father made, confirming his presence and first name. This is sized to the father's plausible land-acquiring window (county organized 1883; homestead period active through circa 1915). A homestead entry will not name the mother directly but will anchor the family geographically and corroborate the census household.

FAN item if the father was foreign-born. Benson County naturalization volumes on FamilySearch (vols. 007785641–007785645, 007785642–007785643) span 1884–1955; they are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable via FamilySearch full-text search. Naturalization declarations and petitions often name the applicant's wife and children, which would be direct parentage evidence for Reuben. Search by surname Spriggs (and Sprigs). If the 1900 or 1910 census shows the father as naturalized or with foreign birthplace, this search becomes higher priority. Also searchable: FamilySearch collection 3241359 (North Dakota Naturalization Records, 1868–1924), 1,883 records, indexed + images.

FAN item: obituaries for Reuben Spencer Spriggs or his close family members often explicitly name parents and siblings. Search the NDSU Obituary Index (library.ndsu.edu/db/obituary/), the Genealogy Trails Benson County obituaries transcription (genealogytrails.com/ndak/benson/obits.html), and Chronicling America for Maddock/Benson County newspapers. ### Jurisdictional Context

Benson County was organized **9 March 1883** from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties, Dakota Territory. It became part of North Dakota upon statehood, **2 November 1889**. Records before that date were created under Dakota Territory; records after, under North Dakota. Maddock is listed as a city with a date range from 1897 onward. County seat is Minnewaukan.
